title: Tennis Star Wins Big After a Last-Minute Call-Up
summary:
Imagine getting a call that you're playing for your country—tomorrow. That's what happened to British tennis player Samuel. He was only told he'd play in the Davis Cup on Friday, after teammate Cameron Norrie pulled out with an arm injury. The next day, he walked into a sold-out arena in London. "It almost felt like a bigger deal than playing any Slam for me," he said.

At first, nerves got to him. He lost the first set 4-6. But then he fought back. He won the second set 6-4, then stormed through the third set 6-1 in just 28 minutes. He dropped only one game in the final set. "This was a big dream of mine," he said. "I got a bit nervous at the start, but I got myself going and I am so happy I got the job done."

His teammate Arthur Fery also had a great day. Fery, who reached the Wimbledon semi-finals this year, was playing at home for the first time since that run. He won his match 7-5, 6-0. He won eight games in a row to beat his opponent. "Coming out as a team in front of all of you guys today in London is unbelievable," Fery told the crowd.

Great Britain now leads 2-0. If Henry Patten and Neal Skupski win Sunday's doubles, Britain will move to the knockout stage for the first time since 2023.
why_it_matters: It shows that being ready for a surprise chance — even when you feel nervous at the start — can turn into one of the biggest moments of your life.
